correctness.rationale: Both original mathematical assertions are true. A fresh exact check in /workspace/branches/check_grid_independent.py uses bipartiteness and König's theorem: at most four vertices per color are allowed, and alpha equals face cardinality minus maximum matching size. This reproduces the eight-entry f-vector and 72,568 nonempty faces. The pivot matching gives 36,039 pairs; a separate complete directed DFS traverses 446,610 covers with no cycles and leaves one vertex and 489 seven-cells. An independent orbit-subset computation gives fixed-face counts (72568,252,444,212) and Lefschetz sums (−488,−30,−12,−14). In degree seven, traces are one minus those sums. For a fixed nonempty face using b orbits the orientation sign times simplicial parity is (−1)^(b−1), so the trace test correctly includes inversions. The four multiplicities are (137,123,114,115). The narrowed claim is reproduced by /workspace/repairs/2/check_grid_reflections.py, including its dual support check. Quotient ranks 260, 251, 252 and 137 follow by rational invariants after barycentric subdivision; these are ordinary orbit spaces. The verification checks no other grid, no integral lattice splitting, and no equivariant homotopy equivalence. Frozen scripts were inspected, not executed.

A four-by-five grid contains interior lattice vertices incident to four unit squares and cannot be grown with just edge-only attachments; at the first step bringing all four squares together the remaining square meets more than one edge or there has already been a corner overlap. The wedge prediction of Conjecture 5 gives neither proof nor reflections.
Chandrakar et al. give total cut classifications on 2×n and on 3×n for k=3, not the present case. The general acyclic element-matching theorem applies nonequivariantly and calculates no character.

evidence: The article gives Betti data rather than stating a homotopy classification for the selected case. However, enumerating all facets from independent five-sets and all their subfaces gives 976007 faces including empty. The article's specified successive element matching leaves exactly 489 dimension-ten faces, with the empty face matched to a vertex. Both row- and column-major conventional lexicographic orders give this result. The appendix guarantees acyclicity and the one-vertex, one-positive-degree wedge conclusion.

Alexander duality shifts degree 10 to 7 on the robust complex. Its full three-skeleton guarantees simple connectivity. Hurewicz and homology Whitehead then imply the ordinary wedge, with no torsion or separate unstable ambiguity. None of this determines fixed-simplex traces; the independent character check requires the actual orbit enumeration.

value.rationale: The single finite grid is a natural unresolved symmetry instance of the robust-clique problem, and row and column reversal form its natural full rectangular symmetry. The exact rational action distinguishes which cycles are invariant under each reflection and the half-turn; it also determines exact rational Betti ranks of the ordinary symmetry quotients. These concrete invariants are not available from the prior ordinary homotopy or rank, and are independently useful without a general-width theorem.
